thread:
incident-bot: INCIDENT - Service discovery SRV failures detected in us-east-1a. PagerDuty: INC1234567. Symptoms: increased SRV NXDOMAIN and timeouts for internal._svc lookups, ~30% of requests failing since 2026-03-15T10:22Z. Auto-page to eng-oncall. See /incidents/INC1234567 for details.
ryan: ACK. I'm on call, grabbing triage. Can everyone avoid wide-scale restarts until we have a plan?
lia: I can start digging. I'm seeing a spike of SRV NXDOMAIN in prometheus: `sum(rate(dns_responses_rcode{rcode="NXDOMAIN",zone="svc.cluster.local"}[1m])) by (zone)` jumped ~x10 at 10:21Z.
sam: consul health shows some grpc timeouts between servers in us-east-1a -> maybe control plane connectivity? Leader still present but increased election latency.
ryan: quick check: are CoreDNS pods in a restart loop in that AZ? `kubectl get pods -n kube-system -o wide | grep coredns` shows several with RESTARTS.
lia: logs from one coredns pod: ```
2026-03-15T10:20:58Z coredns[1]: plugin/errors: 2.3.4: SERVFAIL to 10.0.0.10:53: read udp 10.0.1.23:56543->10.0.0.10:53: i/o timeout
2026-03-15T10:21:02Z coredns[1]: cache: lookup _api._tcp.svc.cluster.local: cache miss
2026-03-15T10:21:07Z coredns[1]: plugin/cache: TTL expired for _api._tcp.svc.cluster.local
2026-03-15T10:21:10Z kernel: nf_conntrack: table full, dropping packet
```
sam: that kernel line stands out — conntrack overflow will cause intermittent UDP failures to upstreams. We're seeing similar on other nodepools after a flurry of ephemeral connections.
ryan: mitigation option 1 (fast): rotate CoreDNS pods in affected AZ to clear local state. Command I'll run: `kubectl -n kube-system rollout restart deployment/coredns --context=us-east-1a` — will do a single-AZ rolling restart. Anyone object?
lia: go ahead. I'll watch logs and metrics.
ryan: running now...
(45s later)
lia: pods are restarting, one by one. seeing GRPC/backoff drop and then healthy connection. A handful of app services recovered already (ingress -> backend SRV lookups succeeded).
jordan: customer-suc: We're seeing 12 active customer incidents tied to embeddings ingestion in us-east-1. Most timeouts map to the earlier window. I'll queue an outbound note once we have final impact.
sam: investigating root: conntrack overflow due to ephemeral client connections from a batch job that ramped up at 10:19Z. Kernel logs show repeated `nf_conntrack: table full` on nodes in the coredns pool. Increasing conntrack and draining nodes to apply new sysctl seems necessary.
ryan: immediate followup: bump conntrack on affected nodes to 262144 and cordon/drain nodes in pool coredns-us-east-1a-*. Commands I applied (runbook snippet): ```
# on each affected node (via kube-ssh)
echo 262144 > /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
sysctl -w net.netfilter.nf_conntrack_max=262144
kubectl drain node/<node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data
```
lia: after bump+restart, SRV lookups are stable. Prometheus alert rate back down to baseline. No more NXDOMAIN spikes for the last 5m.
ryan: pagerduty: ACK by ryan (oncall). Monitoring for 30m then we'll move to postmortem.
pagerduty: Incident INC1234567 acknowledged by ryan at 2026-03-15T10:27Z.
sam: root cause hypothesis: a noisy batch job created a high rate of short-lived connections that exhausted conntrack on nodes hosting CoreDNS, causing UDP timeouts to upstream consul/etcd servers and resulting in SRV resolution failures. Mitigations: (1) increase conntrack as emergency fix, (2) add conntrack autoscaling / alerting, (3) enforce rate limits on batch jobs, (4) pin CoreDNS to nodes with higher conntrack capacity.
lia: I'm starting a short runbook update and adding a dashboard tile for conntrack usage per node. Will also add an alert for `kernel_nf_conntrack_drops_total > 0` aggregated by nodepool.
jordan: customer-suc: sending proactive note to affected customers now, linking to status page and noting mitigation steps.
ryan: handoff: lia needs to head off shift in ~10m. Sam will take lead for the rest of the incident. Lia -> Sam: summary: restarted coredns, bumped conntrack to 262144, drained/rotated affected nodes, SRV resolution restored, watch for recurrence. Runbook link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/dns-conntrack (internal).
lia: handing off. Sam you have the lead. I'm reachable for escalation. :wave:
sam: taking it. I'll keep monitoring and follow up with a bridge for postmortem. Next steps: schedule RCA, update runbook, and push a small HA change to avoid single-AZ exhaustion.
incident-bot: UPDATE - mitigation applied, customer impact reduced. Incident remains open for RCA and monitoring.
ryan: marking incident status as "mitigated" in the incident tracker. Will add timeline and logs to the INC ticket. Good work team.
jordan: will coordinate customer comms and include root cause summary once RCA is ready.
(THREAD END)
